title: Middleware, the codebase & architecture
objective: Learn the one shape every middleware shares (wrap the state creator; wrap set and/or patch the api), tour persist/devtools/immer/redux, then map every concept to the real files and the architecture so you can navigate and extend the code.

quiz.prompt: What is a zustand middleware, structurally?

options.text: A function that takes a state creator and returns a new state creator, wrapping set and/or patching the store api.
A React component that wraps your tree and provides the store via context.
A plugin registered globally that applies to all stores at once.

quiz.prompt: You ship v2 of your app adding `settings: { theme, density }` to a persisted store. Returning users see `density` undefined even though the new default sets it. Why?

options.text: persist never reads old data, so all defaults are lost.
persist’s default merge is shallow — the stored `settings` object overwrites the new default `settings` wholesale, dropping `density`.
